svg.text: CoreFFT chain A (chain B is a second identical instance)
green = hand-written Verilog | red = SmartHLS (the last one in the datapath) | purple = hard IP | grey = memory
Two complete chains run concurrently on disjoint row blocks (SAR_FFTBLK = 64 rows). Everything reaches DDR through
ONE 64-bit port, FIC_0 — so the interconnect, not the kernel count, is the shared resource every optimisation runs into.
CoreFFT sits in a SEPARATE 12.5 MHz domain (SLOWCLK); the gearbox GBX crosses 64-bit @ 100 MHz to its stream rate.
Window and detect have NO block of their own — they are fused into the feeder and the unloader respectively,
which is why the stage table reports 0 s for both: the work happens inside another kernel's existing DDR pass.
